\section[valutare]{valutare — to evaluate, to weigh up}

\label{lesson:IT-C347-valutare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to specify, then the Italian for the clarification.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: valutare}
\textbf{valutare} — \textquotedblleft{}to evaluate, to weigh up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dobbiamo valutare bene i costi prima di comprare la casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We have to weigh up the costs carefully before buying the house.}
\end{quote}

Also to value in money: \emph{valutare un quadro}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{valutare} is built on \emph{valuta} \textquotedblleft{}value\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{valere} \textquotedblleft{}to be worth\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{valēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be strong, to be worth\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{valutare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{valutare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{valutare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to specify, then the Italian for the clarification, then say \emph{valutare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does valutare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To evaluate, to weigh up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[il giudizio]{il giudizio — the judgement; good sense}

\label{lesson:IT-C347-giudizio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the clarification, then the Italian for to evaluate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il giudizio}
\textbf{il giudizio} — \textquotedblleft{}the judgement; good sense\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Non dare un giudizio prima di conoscerlo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do not pass judgement before you know him.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Mettere giudizio} — to grow sensible. \emph{A mio giudizio} — in my judgement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{giudizio} is inherited from Latin \emph{iūdicium} \textquotedblleft{}a trial, a judgement, an opinion\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{iūdex} \textquotedblleft{}a judge\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[giudicare]{giudicare — to judge}

\label{lesson:IT-C347-giudicare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to evaluate, then the Italian for the judgement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: giudicare}
\textbf{giudicare} — \textquotedblleft{}to judge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Non giudicare le persone dai vestiti.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do not judge people by their clothes.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Giudicare qualcuno da qualcosa} — to judge someone by something. A \emph{giudice} judges in court.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{giudicare} is inherited from Latin \emph{iūdicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to judge, to give a ruling\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{iūdex} \textquotedblleft{}a judge\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[oggettivo]{oggettivo — objective}

\label{lesson:IT-C347-oggettivo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the judgement, then the Italian for to judge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: oggettivo}
\textbf{oggettivo} — \textquotedblleft{}objective\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cerco di essere oggettivo, anche se è mio figlio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I try to be objective, even though he is my son.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Oggettivamente} — objectively.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{oggettivo} is a learned borrowing from Medieval Latin \emph{obiectīvus}, from \emph{obiectum} \textquotedblleft{}a thing set before (the mind)\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{obicere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw before\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{iacere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[soggettivo]{soggettivo — subjective}

\label{lesson:IT-C347-soggettivo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to judge, then the Italian for objective.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: soggettivo}
\textbf{soggettivo} — \textquotedblleft{}subjective\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il gusto è soggettivo: a me piace, a te no.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Taste is subjective: I like it, you do not.}
\end{quote}

\emph{È una cosa soggettiva} — it is a matter of taste.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{soggettivo} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{subiectīvus}, from \emph{subiectum} \textquotedblleft{}what is placed under\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{subicere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw under\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{iacere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
